comparison.note: same corpus, same window, same costs, same risk policy, same simulator; the only difference is the exit rule, which is what the comparison is for

context.rule: benchmark BTC daily close against its own 200-day EMA, with that EMA's 20-day change deciding trend from range: BULL when close > EMA200 and the EMA rose over the last 20 days, BEAR when close < EMA200 and it fell, SIDEWAYS otherwise, UNDEFINED while either input is still warming up. This is the project's existing convention (trading_bot/research/swing/backtest.py::build_regimes), reused rather than re-invented; it is a market label for reporting, never a signal.
context.warm_up: the frozen 1h shards continued with the holdout shards before aggregating

instrument_check.note: the runner that produced the new window's figures reproduces the published figures of the consulted windows exactly; a failure here would mean the new reading was taken with a different instrument

net still > 0 with the largest winner removed
net > 0 in at least 2 of 3 time blocks
